video_title: The Macro Show FREE EDITION | Markets, Midterms & The Road to Quad 4
gist: Day-after-midterms Macro Show: Keith McCullough says WTI broke its immediate-term trade (97), so Hedgeye sold all commodity/shipping exposure and rotated into long-duration bonds (ZROZ), positioning for Quad 4 (growth and inflation slowing) in 1H 2027 after an expected inflation peak on the December print. He frames the AI/semis complex as 'the mother of all bubbles' (3x semis ETF SOXL down ~76% from its June peak), argues the 10-year's 5.31% peak matches the October 2007 cycle peak, expects a procyclical Fed hike in December, and names SpaceX as his one election-driven short.

insights.claim: Hedgeye expects US inflation to peak on the December CPI print (released in January) and the economy to move fully into Quad 4, with growth and inflation both decelerating, for the first half of 2027.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Position for slowing growth and inflation: long bonds, short commodities and high beta.
insights.quote: we would expect to go full-blown into quad 4 for the first half of 2027.

insights.claim: Commodities breaking trend is a Quad 4 signal; in Quad 4 investors should be short oil, commodities, energy stocks and high-beta/high-momentum stocks.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Avoid buying 'dips' in energy and momentum during Quad 4.

insights.claim: Hedgeye's Quad 2 regime (accelerating growth and inflation) peaked in Q3/June, and high-beta momentum appropriately rallied into that peak; bounces in it now are selling opportunities.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Treat momentum bounces as exits.

insights.claim: The 10-year BBB corporate spread risk is breaking out after falling through the cycle peak, signaling rising corporate spread risk for leveraged, cyclically sensitive companies.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Reduce exposure to levered cyclicals as credit spreads widen.

insights.claim: Hedgeye is long healthcare, equal-weight S&P 500 and consumer staples (XLP), adding to staples on down days since it is far from a max position, and plans to short bounces in tech.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Defensive sector rotation is Hedgeye's Quad 4 playbook.

insights.claim: WTI broke its immediate-term trade level of 97 (trend at 92); Hedgeye cut energy to a single ~1% Brent position, will exit fully if Brent breaks its 99 trend, and sold all shipping and commodity exposure.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Hedgeye's process signals further oil downside toward the 92 trend test.

insights.claim: When an immediate-term trade breaks, systematic selling accelerates, comparable to a gamma move, raising the probability of testing the trend level; a trade break is not a dip to buy.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Reduce positions to minimum on trade breaks rather than averaging down.
insights.quote: It's not a dip. It's an immediate term trade break.

insights.claim: Gold is a currency, not a commodity, and has the strongest inverse trending correlation with the US dollar; with gold and silver at the low end of their risk ranges, Hedgeye covered some of its precious-metals short.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Dollar direction is the key driver for gold over 90+ day horizons.

insights.claim: Copper is the most recent commodity to break trend; Hedgeye is short copper miners Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) and Southern Copper (SCCO) and calls palladium one of the best commodity crashes it has called.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Copper miners are on Hedgeye's short list.

insights.claim: Hedgeye covered its bond shorts in recent months and is now buying long-duration Treasuries via ZROZ (25+ year) and BNDD, a reversal significant because institutions with trillions in AUM follow its calls.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Long-duration Treasuries are favored entering Quad 4.

insights.claim: The 10-year yield peaked at 5.31% in 2026, exactly matching its 2007 cycle high when the economic and stock market cycle peaked in October; after 2007 the 10-year fell to 1.4% by 2012.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Cycle-peak yields imply a long multi-year decline in rates.
insights.quote: Bond yields peak when the cycle peaks.

insights.claim: The yield curve shows the 30-year in bearish trend, the 10-year neutral (near breaking its 4.91% trend level), and the 2-year bullish, consistent with a December Fed rate hike.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough and Matt Cooper
insights.so_what: Front end prices a hike while the long end prices a slowdown.

insights.claim: Lagging November and December inflation prints will push the Fed to hike in December, which will look like a policy mistake amid imploding AI bubble stocks and AI-related credit, and the Fed will then panic-cut in 2027, perpetuating the panic.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Expect a hawkish-then-dovish Fed whipsaw.

insights.claim: Hedgeye's 10-year yield risk range is 4.88%-5.06%, and it buys long bonds on bounces to lower highs in yields.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Defines tactical entry zones for duration.

insights.claim: The statistic that the S&P 500 was up a year later after the last 19 midterms (e.g., Goldman Sachs election research) is not useful for cycle-aware investors.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Seasonal election stats shouldn't override cycle signals.

insights.claim: There is a 'raging bear market' in AI bubble stocks; the 3x levered semiconductor ETF SOXL peaked near $300 in June and closed at $73.12, down about 76%, which McCullough calls the 'mother of all bubbles.'
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Levered AI/semis exposure carries extreme drawdown risk.

insights.claim: Hedgeye's short list includes AI bubble stocks SoftBank (SFTBY), CoreWeave, neoclouds, Oracle and SpaceX.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Named AI-infrastructure shorts for Quad 4.

insights.claim: Asian AI-linked markets remain in breakdown: Japan fell 1.4% overnight despite the election, South Korea is down 38% from its bubble high, and Taiwan is at three-month lows; Hedgeye is short South Korea, Malaysia and Indonesia.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Asia semis-heavy markets remain short candidates.

insights.claim: With the S&P 500 below its 7,678 negative-gamma level, moves in both directions are faster and self-perpetuating, typical of a developing bear market; it must clear 7,703 (trade) and 7,639 (trend) to signal bullish.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Expect high volatility and avoid chasing rallies.

insights.claim: Short-dated (~10-day) implied volatility jumped to 28 from about 9 two weeks earlier as investors bought puts to hedge the election; once event risk passed, hedge removal plus negative gamma fueled a rally, as after Trump's first election.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough and Matt Cooper
insights.so_what: Post-event hedge unwinds drive short-term relief rallies.

insights.claim: One-month realized volatility rising above three-month realized volatility is a problem because it perpetuates systematic selling, seen most near the semiconductor/AI bubble.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Monitor realized-vol crossover for systematic de-risking.

insights.claim: The QQQs are nowhere near bullish trade and trend and are more likely to be shorted than SPY; only 38% of stocks rose on the S&P 500's first up day in four.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Narrow breadth argues against chasing tech.

insights.claim: SpaceX is Hedgeye's one election trade: a short, because Elon Musk is seen as an election loser who will get less government help in rate-of-change terms, while he may be selling SpaceX to buy Tesla.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Political shift threatens government-dependent Musk ventures.
insights.quote: I think SpaceX is a short uh because it will get less in rate of change terms. Government help.

insights.claim: European equities like disinflation and the German 10-year possibly breaking trend; Hedgeye exited its German short but keeps a French short as France heads toward recession.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye CEO)
insights.so_what: Europe is relative strength on falling yields; France remains weak.
